extracted.intended_audience: reporters, editors, producers and journalists covering trauma-informed topics
extracted.subtask_description: A style guide for news professionals offering evidence-informed, ethical and practical guidance for reporting on trauma, including language, news choices, scientific terminology, and special considerations for trauma-inflected issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-informed guidance on news choices
rubrics_metrics.description: The style guide provides evidence-informed guidance on news choices when reporting on the impact of trauma on individuals, families and communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed as a quick, authoritative reference for reporters, editors and producers (including those working on tight deadlines). Entries are intended to help journalists decide what to cover and how coverage choices affect trauma-exposed people and communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language usage for trauma reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on appropriate language usage when reporting about trauma and its impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes recommendations for wording that is ethical, sensitive and safe; aims to reduce re-traumatization and stigmatizing phrasing. Linked to in-depth tipsheets and examples in the Dart Center resource library.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics in reporting on trauma
rubrics_metrics.description: Baseline ethical standards for how to report on trauma-affected individuals, families and communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames reporting choices around safety, consent, power dynamics and minimizing harm; reflects the Dart Center’s baseline recommendations for best practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate use of psychological and scientific terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations for the appropriate use of relevant psychological and scientific terminology in news coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies when and how to use clinical or scientific terms correctly and responsibly so as not to misrepresent diagnoses, mechanisms, or research findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special considerations for trauma-inflected issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Special considerations when reporting on consequential trauma-inflected issues such as racism and gender-based violence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses intersectional and contextual factors; emphasizes sensitivity and awareness of systemic harms when covering issues that are both traumatic and socially/politically charged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline recommendations for best practice
rubrics_metrics.description: All entries reflect the Dart Center’s baseline recommendations for best practice in trauma-aware journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as a minimum standard for ethical, sensitive reporting; intended to be widely adoptable across newsrooms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science-grounded entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries rooted in trauma science are grounded in evidence-based consensus among experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where guidance invokes trauma science, it relies on expert consensus and empirical evidence rather than anecdote or assumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice-grounded reporting recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries on reporting practices reflect the accumulated recommendations and expertise of Dart Center fellows, Dart Award winners and other journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Represents accumulated professional experience and editorial judgment from practitioners who prioritize ethical, evidence-informed consideration of trauma.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practicality and timeliness (usable under tight deadlines)
rubrics_metrics.description: The guide is intended as a quick, authoritative reference usable by newsroom staff working on tight deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance is concise and actionable to support fast editorial decisions while maintaining trauma-informed standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Living document and feedback-driven evolution
rubrics_metrics.description: The style guide is a living document that welcomes feedback, suggestions and criticism to remain relevant to the global journalism community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users are encouraged to report what guidelines they find useful, what they disagree with, and what’s missing; entries will be continually updated and expanded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking to in-depth tipsheets and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries link to an extensive library of in-depth tipsheets and other resources to support implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide provides entry-level guidance plus pathways to deeper materials (tipsheets, research summaries, practitioner resources) for reporters who need more detail.
